newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine Duhalde says he is No.1 candidate - paper.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Duhalde says he is No.1 candidate - paper.

text.p: The governor of Argentina's most populous province defended his claim to leadership in the race to succeed President Carlos Menem, telling a newspaper he was the top candidate.

Buenos Aires province governor Eduardo Duhalde, who is visiting Spain, was asked by the Clarin newspaper whether he was annoyed by Menem's refusal to recognize him as the only possible Peronist Party candidate for 1999 elections.

"Whether people like it or not, I am the natural Peronist candidate for 1999," Duhalde was quoted by saying by Clarin on Wednesday. Duhalde governs a province accounting for 40 percent of Argentina's population.
Former Formula One racing driver Carlos Reutemann, also a Peronist, announced earlier in the week he was going to run for president, and said that Menem had given him his blessing.
Another celebrity-turned-Peronist governor, Ramon Ortega, a former pop singer who led the Tucuman provincial government, is also running.
Under Argentina's constitution, Menem must step down at the end of his second term of government.
The Peronist Party was founded as a populist movement by Gen. Juan Peron in the 1940s.
But Menem has presided over austere economic reforms which have shriveled inflation and boosted Argentina's economic competitiveness but at the cost of 17.3 percent unemployment.
